picks.name: nxnative
picks.description: Switch games running natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac: an NSP folder becomes an unsigned IPA (NSO rewriter, Horizon HLE host, NVN→Metal)
picks.readmeHead:
# nxnative

Play your own Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 games natively on Apple silicon Macs, iPhone and iPad. One script packs your game into a Mac app or an unsigned IPA that you sideload.

It is not an emulator: the game's own code runs directly on the Apple chip, with Switch graphics rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from any game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo or any game publisher.

[Games](#games) · [Community front ends](#community-front-ends) · [Requirements](#requirements) · [How to play](#how-to-play) · [Discussions](#discussions) · [For developers](#for-developers)

## Games

The full [tested games table](dm/games/README.md#games) includes original Switch games, tested builds, engines and graphics APIs. Each game's note records its tested platforms, progress and known issues.

These Switch 2 games have passed Mac gameplay testing. Build them from a [`.nup` file or a dump folder](#switch-2-games):

- [Donkey Kong Bananza](dm/games/040074A01BF12000/README.md)
- [Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave](dm/games/04007EF01F8AE000/README.md) — up to 120 fps
- [Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment](dm/games/04003F40232DE000/README.md)
- [Kirby Air Riders](dm/games/040077201BE50000/README.md)
- [Mario Kart World](dm/games/0400C3F00006E000/README.md)
- [Mario Tennis Fever](dm/games/0400D4201C6EA000/README.md)
- [Pokémon Pokopia](dm/games/0400A3A01EE4C000/README.md)
- [Splatoon Raiders](dm/games/0400380020056000/README.md)
- [Star Fox](dm/games/0400E88025B1A000/README.md)
- [The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time](dm/games/0400486024DEC000/README.md)
- [Yoshi and the Mysterious Book](dm/games/0400245021D2C000/README.md)

## Community front ends

Community projects build on nxnative with tools to turn your games into apps for your iPhone, iPad or Mac without the command line, and libraries to organize and launch them. They are separate projects: questions and bugs about them go to their own pages.

- [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple)

picks.readmeHead:
# D2R Mobile

**An open-source compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion, for iOS, macOS, Android and HarmonyOS.** It brings the Nintendo Switch release you bought, expansion included, to iPhone, iPad and Mac in full: the original game code runs natively, every control is rebuilt for touch, the frame rate holds at 60 fps, and you are in a game one second after the main menu. There is now a native macOS version as well (first version): on an Apple silicon Mac it starts on double-click and works with keyboard, mouse and gamepad. **Since v2.0 there is an Android version** (community port): the same game program executes natively on ARM64 Android phones, with the graphics reimplemented on Vulkan; on a Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 phone the camp and the Den of Evil and Cow Level fights all run at a median 60 fps (see "Android" below); a HarmonyOS version runs on the same engine (community port: an unsigned shell from the Releases page that you re-sign yourself, nothing to build; see "HarmonyOS"). Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, A15) has a community port (developer preview) that has reached the character-selection screen only on its author's device; see the device table below.

This is not a tech demo that "sort of runs". It is a mobile version polished for daily play, from your first character all the way through the endgame.

Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later; iOS 18 – 25 with the older-API build) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later; macOS 15 – 25 with the older-API build) · Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, A15; community port, developer preview) · Android phones (ARM64, Android 12 or later, Vulkan 1.1; community port) · HarmonyOS phones (HarmonyOS NEXT; community port, unsigned shell from the Releases page that you re-sign yourself) · Game version: Switch release with Reign of the Warlock, 1.0.34.0 (corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012) · English / 中文 / Español / Русский / 한국어 · License: MIT · **Bring your own game files**

picks.description: Ears for coding agents: let AI hear, review and make sound. CPU-only, open source.
picks.readmeHead:
# earshot

**Ears for coding agents.**

<!-- launch video -->
[**Watch the 0.4 launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.4.0) (35 s): its sound effects are
takes from the earshot bank placed with the launch kit, plus the one CC0 recording it shows being re-made, over a
licensed music track. Play every sound in the bank on
[the earshot site](https://leonxlnx.github.io/earshot-site/).

![Frames from the first launch film (0.1)](docs/media/launch_frames.png)

AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.

earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.

With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.

**New in 0.4: the sound of a music-led launch film.** 51 new sounds made in code for the soft, short, mid-register
style those films use: rounded UI pops, wood and plastic knocks, short cut hits and sub hits with a kick, gated
glockenspiel / celesta / marimba notes and chime runs, water drops, camera shutters, reverse cymbals, a thump-whoosh,
short dark risers, bright swishes, burst glitches and mid dings (the bank now holds 252). A new `launch` kit preset
mixes every effect against the music bed instead of at a fixed level, says where each one sits against the cut (taps
lead it, whoosh peaks land after it) and how

picks.name: leanrea
picks.description: One 8 KB skill that replaces REA (Reverse Engineer Anything): plain CLI tools, no MCP. Benchmarked: 38% faster, 35% cheaper.
picks.readmeHead:
# leanrea

**One 8 KB skill file that does what [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) does: no MCP server, no 207 tools, no setup.**

REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) puts an MCP layer between your agent and tools it can already use: asar, otool, nm, `go version -m`, jadx, apktool, Ghidra, tshark, binwalk, sqlite3. leanrea drops that layer. It tells the agent which command is fastest for each kind of target, gives it ready-to-paste recon commands, and lists the traps that REA's code handles for you. The agent then runs the real tools itself.

|  | REA 6.5.0 | leanrea |
|---|---|---|
| What gets installed | 25 MB npm package + MCP server | one `SKILL.md` |
| Instructions | 23.5 KB skill + 48.8 KB references | 8 KB |
| Tools added to the agent | 207 (3.35 MB of definitions) | 0 (uses Bash) |
| Context for "Reply OK", all tools loaded | 400.7k tokens, $1.60 | 34.5k tokens, $0.09 |

## Benchmark

Claude Code headless (`claude -p`), Sonnet 5.5, macOS arm64. 4 reverse-engineering tasks × 3 reps × 3 arms, with the arms run side by side. Answers are graded against hand-made keys.

| arm | total wall time | cost | turns | tokens | score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **leanrea** | **388 s** | **$2.17** | **55** | **2.40 M** | 74/75 |
| no skill | 479 s | $2.21 | 81 | 3.11 M | 67/75 (one refusal) |
| REA (MCP + its skill) | 627 s | $3.36 | 124 | 5.93 M | 75/75 |

Against REA, leanrea had **38% less wall time, 35% lower cost, 56% fewer turns and 60% fewer tokens, at the same accuracy**. Its one partial miss named an older IPC channel instead of the v2 one (both channels exist).

The tasks:
- **electron**: trace a feature through a real Electron app's app.asar (native function → main-process class → IPC channels).
- **native**: inventory the exports, a TCC permission check and the single-instance lock of that app's native addon (`.node`).
- **go**: toolchain and dependency versions of a stripped `gh` binary.
- **deep**: from disassembly alone, the exact socket path format, wire p

picks.name: tstack
picks.description: The agent skills I use every day. Works with Claude Code and Codex.
picks.readmeHead:
# tstack

The agent skills I use every day, cleaned up so anyone can use them. They work
in Claude Code and Codex. Some use [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)
features when they are available and fall back to native tools when they are
not.

## Skills

| Skill | Say | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `full-send` | "full send" | Takes a change to a merged PR with nobody watching: proves it, reviews it, files it, babysits it, merges it. |
| `full-stop` | "full stop" | Same as `full-send`, but stops when the PR is ready for you to merge. |
| `council` | "council" | Gets review from three models from different providers, and loops until they agree. |
| `sol-loop` | "sol loop" | Reviews a change with GPT Sol in a loop until both agents agree. |
| `file-pr` | "file a PR" | Files a short PR that leads with the problem, not an inventory of changes. |
| `takeover` | "take over" | Finishes someone else's PR, branch, or agent thread, and keeps their credit. |
| `babysit-pr` | "babysit" | Watches a PR through CI and review bots, and fixes the real findings. |
| `modernize` | "modernize" | Rebases an old PR and decides if it should still exist. |
| `leaving-pr-comments` | (automatic) | Formats comments that an agent posts on your behalf. |

Some skills call others. Install the ones they need too:

- `full-send` uses `sol-loop`, `file-pr`, and `babysit-pr`.
- `full-stop` uses `full-send`.
- `takeover` uses `modernize`, `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `leaving-pr-comments`.
- `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `modernize` use `leaving-pr-comments`.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/   # Claude Code
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.codex/skills/    # Codex
```

## Requirements

- An authenticated [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`).
- `python3` for `babysit-pr`'s `pr-wait` script.
